recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group later wants more examples for educational clarity, handle that as separate editorial follow-up rather than as a missing application of FHIR-51466.
issue_request: FHIR-51466 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I R6 clarification asking how :above and :below behave for reference search parameters whose target is a canonical element, including whether supplied versions are matched first or only used in a final version comparison. The approved resolution required specified or inferred version schemes, ignore-or-reject handling for unknown schemes, greater-than semantics for :above, less-than semantics for :below, exclusion of versions that match the supplied canonical search, and unordered returned versions.
initial_application: Source commit 4dbcb67f72d1f701f1368db66f7a4b6250456583, merged via HL7/fhir#3967, applied the FHIR-51466 wording to source/search.html for both canonical-target :above and :below subsections.
additional_context: FHIR-52895 supplies the version-matching rules referenced by the FHIR-51466 resolution; current source/references.html contains SemVer, date, URL, and fallback matching rules, while source/search.html links canonical search readers to the References and Versions and canonical-reference guidance. Confluence minutes record the FHIR-I persuasive vote, and direct Zulip search found no conflicting FHIR-51466 discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current active build source already conveys the approved FHIR-51466 semantics, and additional local prose or examples would duplicate nearby canonical version guidance without changing implementer understanding.
